<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let the Rust frontend compute a request's prompt block hashes, so the engine's input thread no longer hashes long prompts while holding the GIL the engine loop needs. Revives the idea of #15652 for the Rust frontend; complementary to #63454 (cheaper engine-side hashing) and related to #43483 (frontend hashes for DP routing). Part of the long-context P/D CPU-overhead work in #63439.

## Claims

- The engine accepts frontend-computed prompt block hashes; prefix-cache hashes are unchanged (byte-identical), so cache hits, KV connectors and KV events are unaffected.
- The Rust frontend covers `sha256` and `sha256_cbor` for plain, LoRA, cache-salt and lookahead (EAGLE) requests; other requests are hashed by the engine as before.
- Removes the GIL-held prompt hashing from the engine's input thread (~50 ms per 227K-token prompt with `sha256`, ~150 ms with `sha256_cbor`), which otherwise stalls the engine loop: +9.6% decode throughput with `sha256` and +39% with `sha256_cbor` on a workload that admits long cached prompts during decode (below).

## Validation

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`: 114 passed. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-llm`: all passed, including known-answer vectors generated from the engine's own `Request` / `get_request_block_hasher`.
- E2E on GB300 with `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, using a test-only engine patch that recomputes the hashes of every request that arrives with frontend hashes and compares them:

| Config | Requests | Hash check | Cached tokens on repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B, `sha256`, LoRA | 12 (plain, salts incl. non-ASCII / 300-byte, short, LoRA, LoRA + salt) | 12/12 match | 5424/5427; a new salt or LoRA starts at 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B, `sha256_cbor`, LoRA | 12 | 12/12 match | same |
| Qwen3-1.7B + EAGLE3 (lookahead 1) | 8 | 8/8 match | same |

Benchmark (GB300, `Qwen3-0.6B`, Rust frontend, CUDA graphs): 64 streaming decode requests while fully prefix-cached 30K-token prompts (token ids, `max_tokens=1`) arrive at 20/s for 40 s. This resembles a P/D decode instance admitting long prompts. Same binaries in both arms; the "engine" arm stops the engine from advertising `prefix_hash_config`. Mean of 2 interleaved rounds (each within 2%):

| Hash | Prompt hashing in | Decode tok/s | ITL mean / p90 / p99 (ms) | Long-request TTFT p50 / p99 (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | engine (main) | 16,870 | 3.77 / 8.36 / 10.10 | 27.6 / 46.1 |
| `sha256` | frontend (this PR) | 18,494 (+9.6%) | 3.44 / 6.51 / 9.83 | 25.6 / 37.8 |
| `sha256_cbor` | engine (main) | 13,244 | 4.80 / 10.41 / 15.64 | 34.9 / 61.1 |
| `sha256_cbor` | frontend (this PR) | 18,366 (+39%) | 3.46 / 6.45 / 10.04 | 25.6 / 35.5 |

The gain depends on how much of the engine loop the hashing displaces: a small model and a high arrival rate of long prompts make it large; larger models see a smaller relative gain.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

Server (both arms): `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --max-num-seqs 256 --prefix-caching-hash-algo {sha256,sha256_cbor} --enable-prompt-tokens-details`. For the engine arm, set `self.prefix_hash_config = None` in `EngineCore.__init__`. Client: 64 concurrent streaming `/v1/completions` (32-token prompt, `max_tokens=2000`, `ignore_eos`), measuring inter-chunk gaps; after warming 8 distinct 30K-token-id prompts into the prefix cache, send them round-robin at 20 req/s with `max_tokens=1` for 40 s.
</details>

## Details

- `EngineCoreReadyResponse.prefix_hash_config` (algorithm, `hash_block_size`, `NONE_HASH`, lookahead) is set when the engine hashes blocks. Sending `NONE_HASH` means frontends needn't reproduce the seed logic.
- `EngineCoreRequest.block_hashes` seeds `Request.block_hashes`; the existing hasher continues from there. The engine only checks the count (`(prompt_len - lookahead) // hash_block_size`) and otherwise hashes the prompt itself.
- The Rust encoder writes pickle protocol 5 / canonical CBOR exactly. It leaves to the engine: multimodal and prompt-embeds requests, `xxhash*`, keys over one 64 KiB pickle frame, and the rare requests whose strings pickle could memoize by identity.
- The Python frontend doesn't send hashes yet.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Pin the engine's prompt block hashes that the Rust frontend reproduces.
+
+The Rust frontend computes prompt block hashes itself (see
+`rust/src/engine-core-client/src/prompt_block_hasher.rs`), and they must be
+byte-identical to the engine's. Its unit tests check them against the vectors
+in `VECTORS`; this test checks that the engine still produces those same
+vectors, so a change to the engine's hashing fails here instead of silently
+splitting the two apart.
+
+If the change is intended, update the Rust hasher to match, then regenerate
+the vectors by running this file directly:
+
+    .venv/bin/python tests/v1/core/test_prompt_block_hash_vectors.py
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import regex as re
+
+import vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils as kv_cache_utils
+from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest
+from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
+from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256, sha256_cbor
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import get_request_block_hasher, init_none_hash
+from vllm.v1.request import Request
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
+VECTORS = (
+    REPO_ROOT
+    / "rust"
+    / "src"
+    / "engine-core-client"
+    / "src"
+    / "tests"
+    / "prompt_block_hash_vectors.json"
+)
+
+HASH_FNS: dict[str, Callable[[Any], bytes]] = {
+    "sha256": sha256,
+    "sha256_cbor": sha256_cbor,
+}
+
+# Token ids at every encoding-width boundary of both the pickle and CBOR
+# encodings.
+EDGE_TOKENS = [0, 1, 23, 24, 255, 256, 65535, 65536, 151_645, 0x7FFF_FFFF]
+
+
+def _case_inputs() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    cases: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    plain_prompts = [
+        (16, EDGE_TOKENS * 3 + [7, 8]),
+        (1, [0, 300, 70000]),
+        (3, EDGE_TOKENS),
+        (24, list(range(100, 150))),
+        (300, [i * 7919 % 200_003 for i in range(650)]),
+    ]
+    extra_keys = [
+        ("plain", None, None),
+        ("lora", ("adapter-a", "/models/adapter-a"), None),
+        ("salt", None, "tenant-1"),
+        # Non-ASCII LoRA strings, and a salt long enough for pickle's 4-byte
+        # string length.
+        ("lora_salt", ("adapter-é", "/m/é"), "s" * 300),
+    ]
+    for hash_algo in HASH_FNS:
+        for block_size, prompt in plain_prompts:
+            cases.append(
+                {
+                    "name": f"plain_block_size_{block_size}",
+                    "hash_algo": hash_algo,
+                    "block_size": block_size,
+                    "num_lookahead_tokens": 0,
+                    "lora": None,
+                    "cache_salt": None,
+                    "prompt_token_ids": prompt,
+                }
+            )
+        for num_lookahead_tokens in (0, 1, 3):
+            for name, lora, cache_salt in extra_keys:
+                cases.append(
+                    {
+                        "name": f"{name}_lookahead_{num_lookahead_tokens}",
+                        "hash_algo": hash_algo,
+                        "block_size": 5,
+                        "num_lookahead_tokens": num_lookahead_tokens,
+                        "lora": (
+                            None if lora is None else {"name": lora[0], "path": lora[1]}
+                        ),
+                        "cache_salt": cache_salt,
+                        "prompt_token_ids": EDGE_TOKENS * 3 + [7, 8],
+                    }
+                )
+    return cases
+
+
+def _engine_block_hashes(case: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
+    """The prompt block hashes of the engine's `Request` for this case."""
+    lora = case["lora"]
+    sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=17)
+    sampling_params.update_from_generation_config({}, eos_token_id=100)
+    request = Request(
+        request_id="0",
+        prompt_token_ids=case["prompt_token_ids"],
+        sampling_params=sampling_params,
+        pooling_params=None,
+        lora_request=(
+            None
+            if lora is None
+            else LoRARequest(
+                lora_name=lora["name"], lora_int_id=1, lora_path=lora["path"]
+            )
+        ),
+        cache_salt=case["cache_salt"],
+        block_hasher=get_request_block_hasher(
+            case["block_size"],
+            HASH_FNS[case["hash_algo"]],
+            case["num_lookahead_tokens"],
+        ),
+    )
+    return [block_hash.hex() for block_hash in request.block_hashes]
+
+
+def _engine_vectors() -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Compute every vector with the engine's default NONE_HASH seed, which is
+    what an engine without PYTHONHASHSEED sends the frontend."""
+    saved_seed = os.environ.pop("PYTHONHASHSEED", None)
+    try:
+        none_hashes: dict[str, str] = {}
+        cases = []
+        for hash_algo, hash_fn in HASH_FNS.items():
+            init_none_hash(hash_fn)
+            none_hashes[hash_algo] = kv_cache_utils.NONE_HASH.hex()
+            for case in _case_inputs():
+                if case["hash_algo"] == hash_algo:
+                    case["block_hashes"] = _engine_block_hashes(case)
+                    cases.append(case)
+    finally:
+        if saved_seed is not None:
+            os.environ["PYTHONHASHSEED"] = saved_seed
+    return {"none_hashes": none_hashes, "cases": cases}
+
+
+def _format(vectors: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
+    text = json.dumps(vectors, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+    # Keep each token id list on one line.
+    text = re.sub(r"\[[\d,\s]+\]", lambda m: json.dumps(json.loads(m[0])), text)
+    return text + "\n"
+
+
+def test_engine_matches_frontend_prompt_block_hash_vectors():
+    assert VECTORS.is_file(), f"missing {VECTORS}"
+    assert json.loads(VECTORS.read_text()) == _engine_vectors(), (

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks @njhill, this looks great! My only concern is that there doesn't seem to be anything to catch if the Rust frontend and the Python engine drift apart in the future, which could be pretty dangerous IMO.

Shall we do something like:

- add unit/regression tests on Python side as well to ensure that both side agree on the same pinned hex vector
- add a debug/test-only "verify" mode where engine also hashes and verifies the result against the one frontend sent
